title: The Vital part of the plan
subtitle: 生命科学 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 生命科学（科学与技术·生物与生命科学）
meta: 主题语境：生命科学（科学与技术·生物与生命科学）　|　核心词汇：vital　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 vital 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1968 the tailor wrote of ① a vital part of the plan in the order, and everybody in the shop said at once that it was ② so vital that nobody in the shop would go near it. Three weeks on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the tailor, who never explained anything, had done it with great care and gone home; it was the vital ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the vital part of the plan that anybody there had ever seen, or so the order for November 1962 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too vital to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the customer who had come to help; the vital ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the needle at the far mirror, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a vital city of the coast, and said that no customer in his right mind would call it ⑥ as vital as the city of the coast they had once had in the old shop. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was vital or not, and he said so.

By 1975 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the order. What the line asked for was ⑦ something vital, and nothing besides. The customer from the next shop called the whole plan ⑧ quite vital; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the order kept the names of the vital ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1978, on the same day, she wrote of another vital part of the plan in the same order, and the work, which took two weeks, seemed ⑨ no less vital than anybody had expected. ⑩ The vital city of the coast that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1980, was the one she could never quite name; the vital ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 至关重要（前置定语 a vital part of the plan：1968 年裁缝在订单簿里记下的那件至关重要的一环）
B. adj. 至关重要／充满活力（两处加强说法：so vital that … 与 no less vital than …）
C. adj. 至关重要／充满活力（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 至关重要（表语 too vital to do：母亲觉得它太至关重要，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 充满活力（前置定语 a vital city of the coast：叔叔把整件事称作一桩充满活力的城市）
F. adj. 充满活力（同级比较 as vital as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩海滨充满活力的城市相比）
G. adj. 充满活力（后置定语 something vital：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 充满活力（受程度副词修饰 quite vital：那位顾客的评价）

items.q: a vital part of the plan
the vital part of the plan that
a vital city of the coast
The vital city of the coast that

answers.why: vital 意为“至关重要”，1968 年裁缝在订单簿里记下的是“一件至关重要的一环”，此处作前置定语 a vital part of the plan。
vital 意为“至关重要”，此处用 so vital that 结构，说它至关重要到裁缝铺里没人敢靠近。
vital 意为“至关重要”，订单簿上 十一月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的至关重要方案中至关重要的一环，等于最高级的说法。
vital 意为“至关重要”，母亲认为这件东西“太至关重要了，谁也用不上”，too vital to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
vital 意为“充满活力”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩充满活力的城市”，此处作前置定语 a vital city of the coast。
vital 意为“充满活力”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩海滨充满活力的城市一样充满活力”，同级比较用 as vital as。
vital 意为“充满活力”，订单簿上那半行字要的是“充满活力的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something vital。
vital 意为“充满活力”，邻裁缝铺来的那位顾客认为这套计划“相当充满活力”，quite 修饰原级 vital。
vital 意为“充满活力”，no less vital than 表示“其充满活力不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之充满活力不亚于任何人的预料。
vital 意为“充满活力”，母亲 1980 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的充满活力城市”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1968 年，裁缝在订单簿里记下了一件至关重要的一环。（a vital part of the plan）
它至关重要到裁缝铺里没有一个人敢靠近。（so vital that …）
母亲觉得它太至关重要，谁也用不上。（too vital to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩充满活力的城市。（a vital city of the coast）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩海滨充满活力的城市一样充满活力。（as vital as …）
到了 1975 年，订单簿上只剩半行字：要的是一件充满活力的东西。（something vital）
answers: In 1968 the tailor wrote of a vital part of the plan in the order.
It was so vital that nobody in the shop would go near it.
My mother thought it too vital to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a vital city of the coast.
He said nobody would call it as vital as the city of the coast they had once had.
By 1975 the order asked for nothing but something vital.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 vital 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1968 the tailor wrote of a vital part of the plan in the order, and nobody forgot it.
It was the vital part of the plan that anybody there had ever seen, or so the order says.
My mother thought it too vital to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a vital city of the coast, and nobody argued with him.
The customer from the next shop called the plan quite vital, and everybody laughed.
The vital ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
